items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: And then we'd run over the tune... Parenti would make his chorus and it would be great, and Barry would play his and it would be great. I'd play one...

ctx.x: Yeah. Yes. Yeah. But what I was getting at on that was that a lot of those arrangements that are from his collection that he left have a lot of string parts written now, is it that he would have just discarded these and not used this part as time went on when people didn't want so many strings. Like, for instance, they have cello parts and viola parts and so forth. What kind of orchestras would have used

all those parts? Would have been in the theaters and so forth? Mr. Robichaux was a very fine musician and a very fine gentleman. And he liked me. I mean we got along great. He was the one that I borrowed the orchestration of the panel often. And I concocted my own arrangement of it, you see. And you'd just have to take the parts. The truth of the matter is, in the Dixieland we didn't write parts. We wrote a lead sheet. Which is? With the chords for the piano playing. I'd have to find me doing better than you, you…
